newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks rise on buying by regional fund.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks rise on buying by regional fund.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on Friday on select buying by a regional fund, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 3.03 points up at 628.59. Development Finance Corporation of Ceylon Ltd rose two rupees to 270, Ceylon Brewery Ltd one to 38, and Sampath Bank Ltd 50 cents to 49.50.

"A regional fund was hand picking stocks which have growth potential in 1997," said a broker who declined to be identified. The buying was not restrained by Colombo's perennial problem of poor liquidity, since a recent rise had made sellers more flexible, he said.

"The all-share's recent rise of about seven points, which is due to good corporate results, has loosened up sellers and shown buyers that they will have to pay a premium to get quantity," said another broker.

Turnover was 75.89 million rupees on 2.2 million shares. The main trades were 455,800 shares of Sampath Bank, 40,300 of Asian Hotels Corporation Ltd and 156,200 shares of Tea Smallhodler Factories Ltd.

Foreign buying was 63.59 million rupees and selling was 49.17 million. "Today's activity can be considered exceptional because the trades just happened to match," said Rohan Fernando, a trader at brokerage CT Smith. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
